sections.title: Your social fears are usually wrong

items.q: Why does social anxiety stick even when people are kind?
items.a: We hold **misplaced beliefs about rejection** and systematically **misread other minds** via egocentrism, stereotyping, and correspondence bias. Fear of rejection is usually **wildly wrong**.

items.q: How wrong are our predictions about outreach?
items.a: People show **pessimistic social expectations** — they underestimate interest in conversation, **compliance with requests** (Flynn & Bohns), and positivity of responses.

items.q: What did Jia Jiang's 100 Days of Rejection show?
items.a: He was accepted on **51/106** outlandish asks; only ~**7** were negative. Takeaway Epley paraphrases: **"Other people are way kinder than I expect."**
**Real-world exposure**, not pretend speeches. Hofmann's point: exposure works because it **changes beliefs about what other people are like** — not because it dulls anxiety circuits.

items.q: How should you frame outreach so it feels safer?
items.a: Treat connection as an **invitation, not a demand**. Start small (office hello walk); if **3 unanswered pings**, stop sticky persistence.

sections.title: Why connection is metabolically expensive to skip

items.q: How costly is social isolation for well-being?
items.a: Gallup/Kahneman-Deaton: isolation hurts well-being ~**7× more** than a **$60K** income swing. Going from **zero → some contact** is the big leap; texting maintains bonds but **doesn't build them**.

items.q: What is the "leaky tire" model of happiness?
items.a: Well-being is less about peak moments and more like a **leaky tire** — string **small moments of connection** (compliments, fist bumps, checkout hellos) across the day.

items.q: Why is hearing a voice better than reading text?
items.a: **Voice conveys the presence of a mind** — pitches sound more intelligent, rational, and hirable when heard. People wrongly prefer writing; voice also reduces partisan dehumanization.

items.q: Can introverts benefit from acting extroverted?
items.a: Yes — extroversion correlates **r≈.5** with positive affect; **acting extroverted** lifts mood even for introverts (Fleeson, Lyubomirsky). Treat social reps like exercise, not destiny.
